sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Contract Research Organization (CRO) for Multinational Drug Trials

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (codified, French-model) with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Constitution Article 2; commercial and investment statutes adopt Anglo-American-inspired company-law mechanics and FATF/World Bank-aligned regulatory standards.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (1982, in force 1986)
Egypt–United Kingdom Promotion and Protection of Investments Agreement (1975)
Agadir Free Trade Agreement among Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia (2004)
Egypt–United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Agreement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 94 of 2005), Articles 102-136 governing Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles and Executive Regulations on incorporation through the General Authority for Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop, Cairo Investor Services Center
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association / Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'sis) endorsed by the General Authority for Investment
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of EGP 50,000 (approximately USD 1,000) must be fully subscribed and deposited into a temporary Egyptian bank account opened in the LLC's name; GAFI requires a capital deposit certificate before issuing incorporation approval. Capital may be in-kind subject to certification rules; foreign-owned CROs may hold capital in hard currency with banking approvals.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and shareholders hereby subscribe fully to the paid-up capital of the Company in accordance with the Articles of Association and Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; and RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [City], Egypt, and the Articles as submitted to the General Authority for Investment be and are hereby adopted; and RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Managing Director, [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Legal Representative, each with authority to execute formation filings, corporate registrations, and obtain clinical trial organization licensure; and all actions taken in furtherance thereof are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Drafting of Constituent Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Investor Services Center (through GAFI electronic portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative company names in English/Arabic through the GAFI e-portal. Obtain name availability certificate. Prepare the standard-form Articles of Association (LLC template) in Arabic, expressly stating the business scope as 'clinical trial CRO management and related professional activities under ISIC 7490'. All founding shareholders must execute the draft before a notary public to authenticate signatures.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid passports or national IDs of all shareholders
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Power of attorney from any foreign corporate shareholder
Brief statement of proposed commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, select the next alternative from the submitted list or file an administrative objection to the GAFI Naming Committee with a revised name list within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Egyptian commercial bank accepting corporate deposits (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account in the name of the LLC after presenting the draft Articles and name approval certificate. Each founder/shareholder transfers the subscribed contribution. For foreign transfers, comply with central bank documentation rules and ensure the inward transfer reference states 'capital contribution'. Obtain a certificate of capital deposit from the bank in the company's name.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name reservation from GAFI
Bank account application forms and AML/KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank seeks further source-of-funds proof, provide signed declarations, bank statements, and audited incorporation funding sources; or redirect the deposit to another licensed Egyptian bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Setting Up of the Statutory Registered Office and Lease Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Notary Public Office and Governorate's Official Valuation Committee (for lease stamping)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute or authenticate a lease agreement for the registered office in Egypt. The lease must be authenticated by the notary and stamped at the Governorate's revenue office. The lease address will become the LLC's official seat and the CRO's operational address. Upload the authenticated lease into the GAFI dossier.
required_dossiers: Landlord title deed or evidence of right
Notarized consent of the landlord for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the lease is challenged as not being a valid commercial premise, secure a corrected use license from the local civil defense office to confirm the premises are fit for clinical trial administration services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Electronic Incorporation Filing and Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Electronic Filing Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into GAFI's incorporation portal, complete the 'Request for Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company' electronic form, and upload all constituent documents, including notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, authenticated lease, and bank statement. Pay the applicable GAFI filing and issuance fee. GAFI will issue the incorporation instrument and company register number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a correction request is issued, rectify the described deficiencies within 15 days through the e-portal; if the objection relates to capital deposit validation, resubmit the bank certificate with an official English/Arabic translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Enrollment and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon GAFI approval, apply to the local Commercial Registry office to enrol the company's commercial registration number. Then visit the Egyptian Tax Authority to register for corporate income tax, value-added tax, stamp duty, and payroll tax. Obtain the tax card and VAT certificate. For foreign-signatory contracts, also register withholding tax obligations.
required_dossiers: Tax registration forms (110/111 and supporting tabs)
Manager's ID/passport and board appointment resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial registry questions registered office validity, present the stamped lease and GAFI-issued approved address. If tax registration is delayed, escalate to the ETA's Large/Medium Taxpayer Center or use the tax ombudsperson procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Publication, Seal Authentication, and Social Insurance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya), the Notary Public, and National Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation summary in the Official Gazette for legal effect. Authenticate the corporate seal and signatory specimens at the notary office. Register all employee contracts (including clinical monitor staff) with the National Social Insurance Authority within three months of incorporation. Finalize the statutory books (share register, minutes book, inventory register) and place with the notary for rubber stamp.
required_dossiers: GAFI approval and Commercial Registry certificate
Articles of Association and resolution appointing officials
Employee contracts and social insurance forms No. 1 & 2
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Official Gazette revises the text, file a corrective publication statement and pay the nominal rectification fee. For social insurance filing rejection, correct employee data in the electronic Social Insurance Portal and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) – Clinical Trials and Medical Products Sector
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Clinical Trial CRO Operating License (Good Clinical Practice / Good Laboratory Practice Compliance Certificate)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Environmental Registration) for office-based CRO management services; Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category A) if the premises include laboratory animal facilities, biosafety level 2/3 units, or hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended and Executive Regulations: wastewater BOD5 ≤ 60 mg/L and COD ≤ 80 mg/L for domestic and light offices; VOC workplace exposure limits ≤ 50 ppm for common solvents; hazardous clinical/biomedical waste must be segregated, collected, and disposed only through licensed waste contractors under Decree No. 670 of 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Authority; structural load and building safety inspection from the Governorate's Engineering Administration; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower covering first aid, bio-safety signage, and emergency evacuation procedures for CRO clinical monitoring staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; e-Tax and e-Invoice portal administered at www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors establishing an Egyptian LLC must submit the standard incorporation and business license documents to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Ministry of Trade and Industry; after incorporation, the LLC applies for a Tax Card and unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) at the competent ETA office by filing Form 113 (or equivalent registration form), attaching the Commercial Registry extract, power of attorney, articles of association, and proof of registered office. VAT registration is made separately on the same ETA portal; the LLC receives a VAT/TIN certificate evidencing capacity to issue valid tax invoices. Non-resident foreign entities without an Egyptian branch or fixed establishment generally are not locally registered for TIN/VAT unless they maintain a permanent establishment, supply taxable services in Egypt, or import into Egypt.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a tax resident juridical entity taxed on worldwide income under Law No. 91 of 2005; for indirect tax purposes the LLC is a taxable person subject to Egyptian VAT rules; no automatic pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or statutory hybrid mismatch elections. An LLC can elect its financial year (calendar year default), elect to carry forward tax losses (companies generally carry forward up to five years), and, if qualifying for group registration, may apply for consolidated tax filing. No entity classification election under Egyptian VAT law exists; VAT recovery is governed by standard input/output VAT mechanics.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable supply turnover (mandatory registration for importers regardless of threshold; voluntary registration is available below threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses above the e-invoicing implementation threshold must issue electronic invoices and e-receipts in a structured XML/JSON format submitted to the ETA's central clearance platform in near-real time. Each e-invoice must carry a valid TIN/VAT ID, encoded product/service code, QR code, and clearing reference issued by the ETA. The system rejects non-compliant invoices and requires API integration through approved communication channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of goods where actual physical export outside Egypt occurs within the statutory deadline, supported by customs export documentation. For cross-border services, including CRO services to a non-resident sponsor outside Egypt, the service must be supplied to a recipient outside Egypt, the beneficiary must not consume the service in Egypt, and the CRO service must demonstrate that the taxable person's export evidence meets ETA guidance. If clinical trial management services are performed in Egypt for Egyptian patients and consumed locally, even for a foreign sponsor, those local portions are normally standard-rated; only services benefitting and used entirely outside Egypt qualify at 0%.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit export zero-rating claims for up to five years and restrospectively reassess VAT at the standard rate if export conditions are not satisfied or goods/services are diverted to local consumption. Penalties include the VAT amount due, late payment penalties, and administrative fines; false declarations or fraudulent documentation may trigger 100% additional tax, criminal penalties, and suspension from the e-invoicing system.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary and exchange-control authority; all foreign-exchange and cross-border treasury operations must be executed through CBE-licensed authorized dealer banks, acting under the Unified Banking Act (Law No. 194 of 2020), CBE foreign-exchange circulars, Egyptian Exchange Control Law (Law No. 80 of 1947), and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, which guarantees the free transfer of invested capital and profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound has been convertible under a unified floating exchange-rate regime since 6 March 2024, supported by the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account transactions, including CRO clinical-trial service fees and milestone payments from non-resident pharmaceutical sponsors, are freely convertible and may be retained in foreign currency. Capital-account convertibility is available for registered foreign direct investment, but only if the inward equity injection is made through an authorized Egyptian bank and registered with the CBE via the bank plus the General Authority for Investment (GAFI); subsequent profit and capital repatriation requires audited financial statements, evidence of Egyptian corporate income-tax payment or a tax-clearance certificate, corporate resolutions, and an arm's-length milestone billing trail matching the clinical-trial contracts. Practical hurdles for an offshore-owned LLC CRO include decentralized bank-level due diligence, mandatory valid tax-card status, potential branch-level delays in currency availability, and strict rejection of any settlement routed through non-authorized intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service-export proceeds, including CRO revenue from foreign sponsors, must be repatriated and credited to an account at an authorized bank in Egypt within 30 days of the contractual invoice due date and within a hard statutory ceiling of 180 days from invoice issuance. The mandatory conversion (surrender) ratio is 0% under the post-float regime, meaning 100% of export receipts may be retained in a foreign-currency account with an authorized bank. Off-shore set-off arrangements, cross-border netting outside banks, or collection through foreign EMI wallets is a statutory exchange-control violation exposing the CRO and its managers to penalties imposed under CBE enforcement powers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Investment Account (USD/EUR/GBP) for capital escrow and export-proceeds retention
EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Account for capital escrow and export-proceeds retention
EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Account with dedicated trade-finance and treasury desk
Multicurrency operational account (EGP/USD/EUR/GBP) aligned with global pharma sponsor banking groups
EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Account
EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary regulated treasury rail. The CBE does not license offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, Revolut Business) as deposit-taking institutions or authorized dealers, and such entities cannot lawfully receive FDI equity injections, hold EGP or USD treasury positions for the Egyptian entity, or act as the collection channel for service-export proceeds under Egyptian exchange control. Domestic fintech payment-service providers operating under Law No. 18 of 2019 have Medium feasibility only for ancillary, low-value disbursements to local clinical trial sites and investigators; they must never be used for capital injections, export-proceeds repatriation, or sponsor milestone collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance. CBE instructions and bank policies require at least one director and, in practice, all signatories plus the ultimate beneficial owner to appear in person at a branch in Egypt for identity verification and a compliance interview; fully remote account opening is not permitted for a foreign-owned LLC. Corporate documents must be notarized and legalized or apostilled, or issued directly by Egyptian authorities, and each additional signatory must undergo the same physical KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity for non-resident shareholders or the offshore sponsor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration charting the full shareholding chain to identifiable individuals; corporate-registry extracts of each intermediate shareholder; passports and proof of residential address of all UBOs; source-of-wealth statements; bank reference letters from the sponsor's home-country bank confirming legitimate commercial standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clinical-trial payments characterized by compliance as unlawful medical commissions or fee-splitting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) / Ministry of Health clinical-trial authorization; executed master clinical-trial agreement with the sponsor; itemized milestone-based fee schedule mapped to the ISIC 7490 CRO service scope; contracts with principal investigators and site agreements; informed-consent and patient-recruitment register evidencing documented services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, lumpy, or unexpected milestone wire transfers from foreign pharmaceutical sponsors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Milestone-linked invoice register; sponsor purchase orders and clinical-trial agreement amendments; audited financial statements of the sponsor; a cash-flow explanation memorandum; historical export-proceeds records demonstrating consistent repatriation through the authorized banking channel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance or thin physical footprint for a licensed CRO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated lease agreement for the registered office and trial-documentation facilities; Egyptian payroll and social-insurance contribution records; tax-card certificate; EDA licensing documentation; professional indemnity insurance policy; organizational chart with resident clinical, regulatory, and finance staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, or adverse-media screening hits on foreign investigators or sub-CRO vendors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial sanctions-database screening reports; OFAC/EU/UN list check certificates; contractual warranties and beneficial-ownership certificates from each counterparty; documented compliance sign-off by the CRO's designated AML compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign-direct-investment equity injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank directly to the LLC's Foreign Currency Investment Account at an authorized Egyptian bank, with the wire purpose code designating 'direct investment / equity contribution / capital increase', accompanied by the GAFI investment certificate, a notarized board or shareholder resolution, and the bank's investment-registration form. The inward transfer must be registered with the authorized bank at the time of credit and reported by the bank to the CBE so that future unrestricted repatriation of profits and liquidation proceeds is contractually and statutorily secured; routing through EMIs, digital-asset platforms, third-party set-offs, or unauthorized money transmitters is strictly non-compliant.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements, including site-investigator payments, CRO subcontractor fees, laboratory and clinical-supply procurement, and pass-through costs reimbursable by sponsors, are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for USD/EUR/GBP and via the CBE RTGS and domestic ACH for EGP. High-value clinical equipment and medical supplies are settled through documentary or standby commercial letters of credit issued by the Egyptian bank against pro-forma invoices and, where applicable, EDA import authorizations; SWIFT MT103 remains the default rail for services, milestone settlements, and professional fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP foreign-exchange forwards with authorized dealer banks, backed by documented trade flows and forecast CRO receivables
USD/EGP foreign-exchange futures contracts listed on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) under CBE-supervised market infrastructure
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) with authorized banks for structural hedging of long-term USD-denominated CRO revenue streams
Bilateral foreign-exchange swaps with authorized banks for short-term liquidity rebalancing between EGP and USD positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Name of annual return, corporate declaration, or franchise filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties and timeline triggering administrative strike-off

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Rules regarding annual confirmation for shareholding transfers
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate rate is 22.5% under Law 91/2005 Article 8, as amended. Accredited micro and small enterprises may elect the simplified turnover-based tax under Law 152/2020, ranging from 0.1% to 1.5% depending on the turnover bracket. No statutory tax holiday applies to clinical-trial CRO activities. Investment Law 72/2017 grants a deduction of up to 50% of eligible fixed investment costs in designated sectors; Contract Research Organization services are not automatically within the designated categories. Scientific research and training expenses are deductible within the ceilings set by the Executive Regulations of Law 91/2005.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return, Form No. 19 (Bayan Darbet al-Sharikat), filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing platform (Veta electronic filing module at apps.incometax.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return filed once per fiscal year; quarterly advance income tax instalments are due within one month after the end of each quarter of the tax period, based on the prior year's final assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year. A company with a 31 December year-end files no later than 30 April; a 30 June year-end files no later than 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue - total billings for clinical trial management, site monitoring, data management, regulatory consulting, and reimbursable sponsor pass-through costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize foreign sponsor revenue at the Central Bank of Egypt selling rate on the milestone invoice date; include intercompany pass-through costs only if contractually reinvoiced; do not include amounts not attributable to Egyptian activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of services - site management fees, investigator grants, laboratory outsourcing, patient recruitment, and central laboratory costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all direct costs with tax-compliant invoices and SWIFT/wire payment records; related-party pass-through costs must satisfy the Egyptian arm's length standard and be backed by a transfer pricing documentation file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or loss - Box 1 less Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident CRO affiliates, the Egyptian LLC must not reflect revenue in Box 1 unless the LLC performs the underlying trial functions and bears the related risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating and administrative expenses - salaries, office rent, utilities, professional fees, insurance, IT systems, and general overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct actual and documented expenses only; head-office general and administrative cost allocations to the Egyptian LLC require an approved cost-allocation methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortization - depreciation of laboratory and office equipment, leasehold improvements, amortization of acquired software and clinical databases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the depreciation rates fixed by the Executive Regulations of Law 91/2005; intangible amortization must be supported by purchase or license agreements with DTA-compliant royalty treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or loss before loss carryforward - Box 3 minus Box 4 and Box 5, with statutory disallowances and allowable deductions applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable profit of the Egyptian LLC is fixed on its separate Egyptian books; the LLC cannot include profits of a foreign sponsor's principal office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilisation - offset of prior-year losses within the 5-year statutory window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses approved on prior year returns; losses may be carried forward for 5 years only; ownership changes may restrict the continuity of the claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offset and before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments for intercompany service fees, mark-ups, and pass-through costs must already be reflected in this figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at statutory rate - taxable income multiplied by 22.5% (or the applicable SME rate under Law 152/2020 for qualifying entities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned LLCs are assessed at the standard 22.5% rate; the applicable rate must be evidenced by the entity's approved SME tax status, if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits - foreign tax credit for sponsor-country withholding taxes, Egyptian WHT credits, payroll tax credits, and investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit claims require a certified statement of foreign taxes and a TRC; the credit cannot exceed the Egyptian CIT attributable to the same foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments and quarterly instalments previously paid during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct all quarterly CIT instalments and any tax collected by payroll or self-collection systems; retain ETA payment receipts to substantiate the entries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due - final balance after subtracting advance payments and credits from the computed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A net refund is settled by the ETA only after a desk review; non-resident-owned LLCs requiring a tax clearance certificate must settle any net tax payable in full before clearance is issued.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a return on time attracts a monthly penalty of 2% of the tax due per month or fraction of a month, capped at 40% of the tax, plus a fixed penalty of EGP 1,000 to EGP 5,000. Late payment of assessed tax attracts a 2% monthly surcharge. Inaccurate or misleading declarations result in an additional tax of up to 30% of the understated amount. Continued non-filing permits the ETA to initiate enforced collection, seizure of bank accounts, and criminal reference under Law 91/2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for cash dividends paid by an Egyptian LLC to a non-resident beneficial owner, under Law 91/2005 Article 56 as amended by Law 25/2022.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home revenue authority for the relevant calendar year; (2) apostille-certify and translate the TRC into Arabic; (3) file the ETA treaty relief application with the certified TRC, an affidavit of beneficial ownership, and the entity's commercial registration at least 30 days before the dividend distribution or remittance. Upon prior ETA approval, the Egyptian LLC withholds the treaty rate at source; if prior approval is not obtained, the statutory 10% is withheld, and the non-resident must apply for a refund through the ETA Ordinary Tax Authority Committee. Typical treaty dividend rates in Egypt's DTA network range from 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to a 20% statutory withholding tax; most Egyptian DTAs reduce the rate to 10%-15%, with some treaties retaining 20%. Interest paid to non-residents is likewise subject to a 20% statutory withholding tax, with typical DTA reduction to 10%-15%. Software licenses, clinical database licenses, and protocol-related IP rights are treated as royalties for Egyptian WHT purposes. The same TRC-based treaty relief protocol applies to royalty and interest payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000. Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 15,000,000,000. Country-by-Country Report is mandatory at the same EGP 15,000,000,000 consolidated group turnover threshold. Below the documentation thresholds, a simplified transfer pricing disclosure statement annexed to Form 19 remains compulsory, with fixed penalties for omission.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime comparable to GCC jurisdictions. However, Law 91/2005 Article 30, as amended by Law 211/2020, empowers the ETA to disregard arrangements lacking economic substance, apply the substance-over-form doctrine, and recharacterize intercompany transactions that do not reflect commercial reality. A clinical-trial CRO must demonstrate substantive local operations: physical office premises, qualified clinical staff, local ethics committee approvals, trial master files, and active decision-making on protocol execution. Absence of substance may trigger deemed distributions, full CIT assessment on artificial profits, WHT reclassification, and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of sponsor revenue, use of forged clinical-trial expense invoices, destruction of trial account books, or misclassification of taxable service fees as loans or equity contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment plus a fine of up to three times the evaded tax under Law 91/2005 Article 133; compulsory payment of the evaded tax with a 2% monthly surcharge; revocation of tax clearance and VAT certificates; exclusion from public tenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers, and legal representatives who participate in, order, or conceal evasion are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, fines, and surcharges. Travel bans, asset freezes, and confiscation orders may be imposed; criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an Egyptian LLC solely to bill clinical-trial services or collect dividends without real local staff, premises, trial infrastructure, or decision-making authority, while the substantive activity occurs abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA disregards the corporate form under the general anti-abuse rule; intercompany deductions are disallowed; the LLC is assessed at 22.5% CIT on deemed reconstructed profit; unpaid WHT is recaptured with 2% monthly late penalties; treaty relief is denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate veil is pierced for fraud or abusive reliance on legal personality, directors are personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and withholding amounts; civil restitution orders and suspension from board service apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare the Local File or to file the TP disclosure with Form 19; charging non-arm's length management fees or excessive mark-ups to foreign sponsor affiliates; absence of a written intercompany service agreement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA transfer pricing adjustments under Article 30; additional CIT at 22.5% on adjusted profit; administrative penalty of up to 5% of the adjusted transaction value; 2% monthly late payment surcharge; fixed penalties for failure to submit TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP declarations are jointly liable for the aggregate adjustment, the additional CIT, and the resulting penalties; automatic disqualification from obtaining tax clearance and government approvals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident without collecting the statutory 10% dividend WHT or 20% royalty/interest WHT; distributing profits disguised as intercompany shareholder loans or reinvoicing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A penalty equal to the uncollected WHT, plus a 2% monthly surcharge for each month of delay; the ETA may sequester bank accounts and offset any due refunds against the unpaid WHT liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Article 141 of Law 91/2005 imposes joint and several liability on legal representatives for the tax that should have been withheld and remitted; personal civil restitution and travel bans follow continued non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving sponsor settlement through opaque shell entities in low-tax jurisdictions, processing SWIFT wires without client due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions related to clinical-trial funding, or integrating trial payments into undisclosed connected accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under AML Law 80/2016, as amended: fines up to EGP 5,000,000, asset forfeiture, compulsory dissolution of the entity, and criminal prosecution of the compliance officer and board members.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines, imprisonment of up to 5 years, seizure of personal assets, and prohibition from leaving the country through immigration travel bans at the request of the Money Laundering Prosecution.
